snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic when scale or debris restricts flow through the radiator core. With the engine at operating temperature and the thermostat open, use an infrared thermometer to compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: replace the radiator and flush the cooling system.

snippets.title: Internal coolant loss at intake manifold gasket
snippets.text: Applies to 3.4L V6 engines, model years 2020-2022. Coolant loss with no external leak may come from the intake manifold gasket at a coolant passage. snippets.title: Overflow and reservoir vent check after overheating
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Coolant loss that appears only after the temperature gauge has climbed past normal during towing or mountain driving is usually coolant pushed out through the overflow. Check the overflow hose routing and the reservoir vent for kinks.

Mist water over the coils with the engine idling and watch for arcing at the coil boots in a dark shop. Repair: install updated coil boots and apply dielectric grease.

Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.text: Applies to engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

snippets.title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2014-2020. Repair: update the transmission control software.

snippets.title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with coil-on-plug ignition. A misfire may occur at idle or light throttle only during rain or after a car wash, and it clears once the engine bay dries. Mist water over the coils with the engine idling and watch for arcing at the coil boots in a dark shop. Repair: install updated coil boots and apply dielectric grease.

messages.content: Customer vehicle: 2013 full-size pickup, 5.5L V8, 132,795 mi. The check engine light flashes when I accelerate hard or climb hills, and it stored P0304 (cylinder 4 misfire). Idle is smooth, and it does it in dry weather too. What's the best first check?

Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling [TSB-7808]. That result will show whether this area is involved.
The plug from that cylinder looks clean and is gapped right, no tracking on the porcelain.

That rules that area out. Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank [SM 8.9.8].
Hooked up a spark tester at 25 kV. Strong blue spark every time. So it must be the ignition coil. Just tell me to replace it.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the engine idling in drive and the brake applied, line pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2010-2016. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

messages.content: Quick one, and I just want the part name. 2013 full-size pickup, 5.5-liter V8, 85k miles. Upshifts are harsh, especially 2-3, and there's a delay before it engages. It gets worse the longer I drive. Is it the torque converter? A simple yes or no is fine.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines with electric radiator fans (not the 5.5L V8). Coolant temperature may climb at idle and in slow traffic while it stays normal at highway speed if the radiator fan does not run. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Turbocharger coolant line inspection
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. With the engine cold, inspect the turbocharger coolant return line fitting and the line for dried coolant residue. Residue at the fitting accounts for slow coolant loss with no drips under the vehicle.

messages.content: My full-size pickup is a 2020 with the 5.5L V8 and 59,430 on the clock. I have to top off the coolant reservoir every week or two. There are no puddles under the car and it has never overheated. What's the first thing to look at?

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test

snippets.text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

messages.content: Vehicle is a 2014 compact sedan with the 1.8-liter engine. Odometer shows 151k. It runs hot at idle. In stop-and-go traffic the gauge creeps up past the middle, but on the highway it stays right where it should.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check

The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

messages.content: My full-size pickup is a 2018 with the 5.5L V8 and 189,913 on the clock. Hard, delayed shifts once the car is warm. The first few miles cold are actually smoother. What would you look at first?

Thanks, that helps narrow it down. With the brake held firmly, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine for lift or a gap at any mount [SB 10-847].

snippets.title: Coolant loss with no visible leak from an early-venting cap

snippets.title: Combustion leak (block) test

snippets.title: Overflow and reservoir vent check after overheating
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Coolant loss that appears only after the temperature gauge has climbed past normal during towing or mountain driving is usually coolant pushed out through the overflow. Check the overflow hose routing and the reservoir vent for kinks.

messages.content: Customer vehicle: 2017 small crossover, 1.4L turbo four, 87,841 mi. Coolant keeps disappearing, maybe half a liter every couple of weeks. No drips on the driveway, no steam, and the temp gauge stays normal. How do I start tracking this down?

snippets.title: Flickering lights from a failed alternator diode
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Headlights may flicker or dim at idle because a failed rectifier diode reduces alternator output. snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Repair: install revised front rotors.

snippets.title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with an EVAP purge valve. snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Some vehicles may crank for several seconds before starting on a hot restart because the engine is overfueled. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. If the engine starts noticeably faster in clear-flood mode, it is being overfueled on hot restarts. Repair: correct the overfueling source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from intake manifold gasket shrinkage
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2021-2023, with the revised composite intake manifold. P0171 may set at idle after a cold soak because the manifold-to-head gasket shrinks at low temperature. Smoke-test the intake with the engine cold, concentrating on the manifold-to-head joint. Repair: replace the intake manifold gasket with the updated part.

snippets.title: Fuel pump relay check for delayed prime
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. If restarts are delayed after towing or extended idling in hot weather, check the fuel pump relay terminals for discoloration and record fuel pressure during the first crank. Pressure that rises slowly on a hot restart points to worn relay contacts delaying pump prime.

messages.content: I have a 2018 midsize SUV with the 3.4-liter V6, about 71,829 miles. CEL came on with P0171. It idles rough at stoplights and stumbles a little right after a cold start, but it pulls fine on the highway. My brother-in-law says replace the fuel injector. Is he right?

snippets.title: Slow cranking on a hot engine
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If the engine turns over noticeably slower when hot than when cold, measure starter current draw with an inductive clamp while cranking with fuel disabled. snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

snippets.title: Cold-weather cranking capacity check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If a battery that is healthy in mild weather does not crank the engine after sitting overnight below 0 deg F, with no parasitic draw present, compare the battery's cold cranking rating with the engine requirement and check whether a block heater is fitted and used. This check covers cold-soak no-starts only.

snippets.title: Battery drain from infotainment head unit
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. Repair: update the head unit software.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for several days because a control module or accessory circuit does not go to sleep. Connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal without breaking the circuit. Draw should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate the circuit that stays awake by pulling fuses and correct the fault.

Lateral runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it on the vehicle.

snippets.title: Charging voltage test under load
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play.

snippets.title: Outer CV joint inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. snippets.title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts. A clunk or pop from the front over bumps or while turning at low speed may come from a worn strut upper mount or mount bearing. With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on the strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn the steering lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop at the mount bearing. Repair: replace the strut upper mounts and bearings.

messages.content: Vehicle is a 2012 midsize sedan with the 3.5-liter V6. Odometer shows 74k. The front right side knocks over bumps, even small ones, driving straight at low speed. Turning at full lock is quiet. Where should I begin with this?

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Belt and tensioner check for a battery lamp at cold startup
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. If the battery warning lamp lights for the first minute after a start below 10 deg F, with a short belt squeal that clears once the engine warms, inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. A tensioner that bounces when cold lets the belt slip briefly.

snippets.title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2014-2020. A harsh 1-2 upshift may occur only during the first few minutes of driving below 40 deg F and stop once the transmission warms. Review the transmission fluid temperature reading during the event. Repair: update the transmission control software.

snippets.title: Battery monitoring sensor check, auto start-stop
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. On vehicles driven mostly on trips under 10 minutes that show a low battery message, check the battery monitoring sensor data with a scan tool. A sensor that reports a low state of charge limits charging and keeps the battery low.

snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

messages.content: It's a 2017 compact sedan, 1.8L four-cylinder, roughly 39k miles. Misfire code P0302. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. On top of that, if the car sits for two or three days, the battery is dead. It starts fine with a jump and drives normally, and the weather has been mild. The passenger window is slow going up. Don't give me a test. Tell me the most likely bad part and I'll put a new one in.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for two to three days because the audio module fails to enter sleep mode. After the vehicle has been locked for 60 minutes, measure draw at the negative battery terminal and note whether it drops below 50 mA when the radio fuse is pulled. Repair: reprogram the audio module.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Turbocharger coolant line inspection
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. With the engine cold, inspect the turbocharger coolant return line fitting and the line for dried coolant residue. Residue at the fitting accounts for slow coolant loss with no drips under the vehicle.
